outline:
國際合作專題特論乃透過國際大師的講課，讓學生學習材料科學或資源工程相關領域的重要知識及了解最先進之研究成果或最新開發成品。
This course will provide important information regarding to the latest development or application in the materials science and mineral engineering. Speakers being invited are well-known international scholars in the related area.

The course will emphasize the interplay between crystallography, bonding, and properties. In particular the physical origin of a number of properties, including thermal expansion, thermal conductivity, the refractive index, optical activity, piezoelectricity, and a variety of magnetic and electrical properties will be discussed.  In each case, the tie will be made to the underlying structural features which control the magnitude of the property coefficients (not just the existence of the response as defined by Neumann’s law). Emphasis will be placed on the systematics of designing the response of materials. In addition, several of the fundamentals of crystal chemistry beyond Pauling’s rules, including bond valence sums and crystal field theory will be introduced. Throughout the course the lecture material will be augmented by crystal structure building to illustrate the fundamental concepts.
schedule:
(1)	Introduction (05/30; 2 hr)
(2)	To describe the crystal structure of important materials and to be able to build their atomic models (e.g. calcite, corundum, cordierite, rutile, tridymite and cristobalite with their stuffed derivatives, spinels, β-silicon nitride, perovskite, wurtzite, quartz). (05/30-05/31; 6 hr)
(3)	To understand how physical and chemical properties are related to crystal structure and microstructure. (05/31-06/01; 6 hr)
(4)	To appreciate the engineering significance of these ideas. (06/02; 4 hr)
(5)	Conclusions (06/02; 1 hr)
